paper.title: Algorithm 724: FINV, F-percentage points (Collected Algorithms from ACM)
paper.venue: ACM Transactions on Mathematical Software 19(4), pp. 481-483 (December 1993), Algorithm 724
paper.url: https://netlib.org/toms/724.gz (article DOI not verified by scout; ACM page not fetched)

code.commit: netlib TOMS archive 724.gz (Fortran FINV function and its test driver TEST, with the driver's output listing in comments)
code.archive: sha256 c63388b4b9ec6b2d662e9ea6d772fcf2707e028c9e99a7455db37dccd9111ac2 (downloaded by scout 2026-11-27, 8069 bytes; decompresses to 917 lines)
code.note: Build FINV and the driver TEST from the archive text (the driver writes TESTDATA; it needs no input). The claim is the single table cell for P = 0.90, M = 10, N = 10 in the TEST output block.

claim.location: Shipped test-driver output, the 'Output from test driver TEST' block in the archive comments (decompressed lines ~646-690): the first table, P = 0.90, in the group of columns N:M = 1, 2, 3, 10. The printed row for N = 10 is the cell in column M = 10: 0.23226039E+001. The same value appears in the 'My output' block the author prints after it.
claim.metric: FINV(M=10, N=10, P=0.9), the F-percentage point, compared as a number
claim.determinism: deterministic (the function and the table inputs are fixed; no random input)

tolerance.basis: Fixed before any run. The printed value has 8 significant figures, so its rounding step is 1e-7; a rerun on IEEE arithmetic that rounds the other way differs by one unit. 2e-7 allows one unit of change in either direction, about 1e-7 relative, and nothing larger. Not to be loosened after any run.

cost.cpu_minutes_estimate: Under 1 minute: a few thousand evaluations of FINV.
cost.data_size: None: the driver generates its own inputs.
cost.data_licence: No data. The archive licence is not stated; the rerun should record it.

why: The authors' own test driver prints a table of F-percentage points computed by FINV's iteration, and the number needs the algorithm to compute, so it tests the old Fortran code rather than a closed form (no closed form exists for these percentage points).
